questions.prompt: What can be concluded here about the sale of a milk round?

options.text: A round was priced by the number of houses on it, and the plant was valued on top of that.
Because the plant was valued on its own, what a buyer paid turned mainly on the debts against the houses.
Once the thirteen weeks were up, the buyer alone carried the loss of a house that left.
Any house could change roundsmen overnight, which kept the price of milk in the town down.
